paragraphs.en: Of course, Dunlop's foreignness also sets her apart.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，邓禄普的外国人身份也让她与众不同。

paragraphs.en: In the extensive coverage of her work and life in the Chinese media, she is "the Cambridge graduate who came to China to cook", "the English person with a Chinese stomach", "the foreigner who understands Chinese food best".
paragraphs.zh: 在中国媒体对她工作与生活的广泛报道中，她被称作"从剑桥毕业来中国做饭的才女"、"长着中国胃的英国人"、"最懂中餐的外国姑娘"。

paragraphs.en: "She lends legitimacy to Chinese culture and Chinese cooking at a time when Chinese people really need that affirmation," Tzui Chuang, a Taiwanese-American food writer, told me.
paragraphs.zh: "在中国人非常需要这种肯定的时刻，她为中国文化和中餐赋予了正当性，"美籍台湾裔美食作家崔庄这样告诉我。

paragraphs.en: One of Dunlop's goals is to rescue Chinese food from its reputation in the west as "popular, but … Cheap, low-status and junky".
paragraphs.zh: 邓洛普的目标之一是将中餐从西方人眼中"受欢迎但……廉价、低档、劣质"的固有印象中解救出来。

paragraphs.en: As she explains in Invitation to a Banquet, the earliest Chinese restaurateurs abroad – beginning with those who went to California during the Gold Rush in the 1840s – were uneducated labourers with no culinary training.
paragraphs.zh: 正如她在《宴会邀请》中所解释的那样，最早在海外经营中餐馆的人——从19世纪40年代淘金热期间前往加利福尼亚的那些人开始——都是没有受过教育、也未接受过烹饪培训的劳工。

paragraphs.en: The dishes that they made, like deep-fried wontons and sweet-and-sour everything, were nothing like the sophisticated cuisine back home.
paragraphs.zh: 他们做的菜，比如炸馄饨和酸甜口味的一切，和家乡精致的菜肴完全不同。

paragraphs.en: Chinese food in the west remained a "bastardised form of Cantonese cuisine", and this fed a stereotype of the Chinese as slovenly and undiscriminating eaters.
paragraphs.zh: 西方的中餐长期被视为"粤菜的劣化版本"，这种偏见进一步固化了中国人邋遢且饮食不讲究的刻板印象。

paragraphs.en: Lord Macartney, the leader of a 1793 British diplomatic mission to China, described the Chinese as "foul feeders and eaters of garlic and strong-scented vegetables".
paragraphs.zh: 1793年英国访华使团团长马戛尔尼曾形容中国人“食不厌精、嗜蒜及气味浓烈之菜”。

paragraphs.en: In 2002, the Daily Mail called Chinese food "the dodgiest in the world, created by a nation that eats bats, snakes, monkeys, bears' paws, birds' nests, sharks' fins, ducks' tongues and chickens' feet".
paragraphs.zh: 2002年，《每日邮报》曾将中餐称为"全球最可疑的饮食"，并声称这是"一个食用蝙蝠、蛇、猴子、熊掌、燕窝、鱼翅、鸭舌和鸡爪的民族创造的"。

paragraphs.en: More recently, the possibility that the Covid-19 virus emerged in a Chinese market that sold wild animals revived the old "Chinese will eat anything" tropes, though Dunlop notes that consumption of exotic species is limited to a tiny subset of the population and is controversial in China, too.
paragraphs.zh: 近期，新冠病毒可能源自一家售卖野生动物的中国市场的说法，让"中国人什么都吃"的陈词滥调再度甚嚣尘上。不过邓洛普指出，食用野味的行为仅局限于极少数人群，即便在中国本土也备受争议。

paragraphs.en: She takes pains to point out that the Chinese are discerning about ingredients and have always emphasised the links between food and health.
paragraphs.zh: 她煞费苦心地指出中国人对食材非常讲究，且一贯重视食物与健康之间的联系。

paragraphs.en: The quest for nutritious produce in China created a far more diverse array of foods than is known in the west.
paragraphs.zh: 中国对营养农产品的追求催生了远比西方所知更为丰富多样的食物种类。

paragraphs.en: Dunlop devotes five pages to the "vast clan of cabbages" before moving on to "the punchy alliums, the tribe of onions and garlics", and then to bamboo shoots, roots and tubers, gourds, mushrooms and seaweeds.
paragraphs.zh: 邓禄普用五页篇幅介绍了"庞大的卷心菜家族"，接着转向"辛辣的葱属植物——洋葱和大蒜的族群"，然后是竹笋、根茎类、葫芦、蘑菇以及海藻。

paragraphs.en: She explores the unfamiliar world of vegetables that are harvested from the water, such as water chestnuts and lotus plants, a category that doesn't exist in western cooking.
paragraphs.zh: 她探索着从水中收获的陌生蔬菜世界，比如菱角和莲藕，这些在西方烹饪中并不存在的类别。

paragraphs.en: She describes the fantastic range of flavours and textures that the Chinese have wrought from tofu, which can be silken or firm, smoked or spiced, stir-fried, deep-fried, frozen, toasted, pressed into sheets, soaked in brine or moulded and fermented into "a delicious state of dishevelment, as high and wild as stilton on the brink between ripeness and decay" – a reminder of the double standards that have made western gourmets devalue Chinese food in favour of their own.
paragraphs.zh: 她描述了中国人在豆腐上创造出的丰富多样的口感和质地——或柔滑或紧实、或烟熏或香辣、可快炒可油炸、能冷冻能烘烤、压成豆皮、浸入卤水，甚至发酵成"一种美味的不修边幅状态，如同斯蒂尔顿奶酪在成熟与腐败临界点时那般狂野奔放"。这番描述恰揭示了西方美食家的双重标准：他们贬低中餐的同时，却对自身文化中类似的发酵食品推崇备至。

paragraphs.en: Dunlop also traces the surprising openness of the Chinese to foreign foods throughout history.
paragraphs.zh: 邓禄普还追溯了中国人历史上对外国食品出人意料的开放态度。

paragraphs.en: (Her scholarship builds on Food in Chinese Culture, a classic 1977 study of Chinese food history edited by the archaeologist KC Chang.)
paragraphs.zh: (她的学术研究以考古学家张光直主编的1977年中国饮食史经典研究《中国文化中的饮食》为基础。)

paragraphs.en: During the Han dynasty, which lasted from 206BC to AD220, exotic foods such as grapes, pomegranates, walnuts, sesame, onions, peas, alfalfa, coriander and cucumbers entered the country from central Asia.
paragraphs.zh: 公元前206年至公元220年的汉朝时期，葡萄、石榴、核桃、芝麻、洋葱、豌豆、苜蓿、香菜和黄瓜等异域食物从中亚传入中国。

paragraphs.en: In the Ming dynasty, which lasted from the mid-14th to the mid-17th century and was known for its isolationist policies, corn, peanuts, white potatoes and sweet potatoes arrived from the new world.
paragraphs.zh: 明朝以闭关锁国政策闻名，从14世纪中叶延续至17世纪中叶，在此期间玉米、花生、白薯和甘薯从新大陆传入中国。

paragraphs.en: Two other new world transplants, the chilli pepper and the tomato, were adopted more recently and further transformed the cuisine.
paragraphs.zh: 另外两种来自新大陆的移植作物——辣椒和番茄——在更近的年代被采用，并进一步改变了烹饪方式。

paragraphs.en: For a long time historians assumed that Chinese cooking developed its enormous variety because people had to make the most of scarce resources.
paragraphs.zh: 长期以来历史学家一直认为中国烹饪之所以种类繁多是因为人们必须充分利用稀缺的资源

paragraphs.en: More recent scholarship suggests that the centrality of food drove innovation.
paragraphs.zh: 最新研究指出，食物的核心地位推动了创新。

paragraphs.en: Dunlop underscores the value that the Chinese have always placed on culinary ingenuity: pragmatism and pleasure, not poverty, were always the impetus.
paragraphs.zh: 邓禄普强调中国人历来重视烹饪智慧：实用与乐趣才是其动力源泉，而非匮乏。

paragraphs.en: To understand the Chinese through their culinary history is also to see them in their best lights – as inventive, adaptable, egalitarian and open-minded.
paragraphs.zh: 透过中华饮食文化的历史长河来理解中国人，往往能窥见他们最美好的特质——勇于创新、善于变通、崇尚平等、胸怀开阔。

paragraphs.en: Maybe only a foreigner can see this and say this.
paragraphs.zh: 或许只有外国人才能看到并说出这一点。
